paper_title: White dwarfs as a probe of exceptionally light QCD axions
suggested_experiment_name: White Dwarf mass-radius relation (light QCD axion sourcing)
coupling_convention: Data points are [f_a in GeV, m_a in eV], converted from the plotted axes log10(m_phi/eV) (x) and log10(GeV/f) (y); the 'lower boundary' is the bottom edge of the red White-Dwarf exclusion region (largest excluded f at each mass)
notes: Paper derives NEW observational bounds on exceptionally light QCD axions ('epsilon-model', potential V = -eps*m_pi^2*f_pi^2[cos(phi/f)-1]) from the white dwarf mass-radius relation gap; bound does NOT require axion dark matter (no DM density assumption). Explicit 95% CL text results: for f << 1e9 GeV, excluded 2e-20 < eps < 2e-7 (Eq. 15/B3); for eps << 2e-20, excluded 5.5e9 < f/GeV < 1.1e16 (Eq. 17/B4). Main exclusion plot (Fig. 1) is in the axion parameter space (m_a vs f plane), hence AxionMass type. The excluded region is 2D: I converted the eps bounds to m_a using m_a^2 = eps*m_pi^2*f_pi^2/f^2 (m_pi=135 MeV, f_pi=93 MeV) and emitted approximate polygon corner points. First four points trace the upper-mass boundary (eps=2e-7); remaining points close the region: for f in [5.5e9, 1.1e16] GeV the exclusion extends to arbitrarily small m_a (eps -> 0), represented by sentinel m_a=1e-22 eV; the eps=2e-20 lower boundary applies at smaller f. Exact contour near f ~ 1e16 GeV (where f*eps^{-1/3} ~ M_P) is only approximate since it was derived from Fig. 1, which was not numerically readable. A ZN-model exclusion 33 <= N <= 69 is also given (Fig. 12). Projection (orange dashed, Chandrasekhar-limit WDs) also shown but the primary result is an observed limit. Confidence moderate: region is 2D and points are reconstructed from text formulas, not a table. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 36)) | Vision: Fig. 1 (epsilon-model) traced; the constraint does not require axion dark matter. Flat bottom edge fixed by quoted bound f < 1.1e16 GeV (95% CL); diagonal edge fixed by quoted epsilon < 2e-7 (95% CL) via m = sqrt(eps)*m_pi*f_pi/f, giving log10(GeV/f) = log10(m/eV) - 3.75, in good agreement with the pixel positions of the red region boundary. Fig. 12 shows the analogous Z_N-model bound (33 <= N <= 69).
